title: Where Portland's Creative, Coffee-Lingering Music Fans Cluster: Mapping Spinback's Ideal Neighborhoods
subtitle: A Demographic Analysis of Oregon / Portland Urban Areas

summary.narrative: Across the 21 Portland-area ZIPs analyzed, the region shows a strongly educated, self-employed core: Multnomah County alone holds 444,895 residents with 51.8% college-educated and 15.2% self-employed, and Portland's median age of 39.7 sits squarely within Spinback's 20-45 target. The strongest concentrations of young creatives cluster in close-in eastside and inner-Portland ZIPs like 97214 (27.8% in their 30s, 39.5% bachelor's, 18.1% self-employed), 97209 (30.6% in their 30s), 97227 (32.3% in their 30s), and 97202/97212 (17% self-employed and above), which combine high 20s-40s density, elevated education, and self-employment. These neighborhoods also carry substantial spending power, with 97212 at 44.3% and 97215 at 38.8% earning $150k+, making them the highest-priority siting candidates.

sections.title: The Regional Landscape: Portland's Educated, Self-Employed Core
sections.subtitle: Comparing Multnomah, Washington, and Clackamas counties and the City of Portland on the traits that define Spinback's ideal customer
sections.description:
Spinback Records & Coffee targets music enthusiasts aged 20–45 — creatives, students, and remote workers who linger over coffee. Three signals in the data reveal where that customer concentrates: high college attainment (creative, culturally engaged consumers), elevated self-employment (freelancers and remote workers who treat a cafe as an office), and healthy labor force participation with disposable income to spend on vinyl, gear, and specialty coffee.

Across the three-county footprint, Multnomah County — the urban heart of Portland — stands out as the strongest fit. It combines the highest college attainment (51.8%), the highest self-employment rate (15.2%), the strongest labor force participation (70.6%), and the youngest median age (38.7). Washington County posts a comparable college rate (50.3%) and the highest median household income of the three ($103,133), but its lower self-employment (12.4%), lower labor force participation (65.7%), and older median age (42.5) make it a secondary, suburban-leaning market. Clackamas County trails on nearly every creative-customer indicator: lowest college attainment (38.6%), lowest self-employment (11.0%), and an older median age (42.2).

The City of Portland itself — the client's stated urban core — mirrors Multnomah closely: 50.1% college-educated, 14.3% self-employed, a young median age of 39.7, and a median household income of $91,594. This alignment confirms that Spinback's business model is best supported inside the city proper, where educated, independent, working-age residents are densest.

Business takeaway: prioritize Multnomah County / City of Portland locations. The urban core delivers the rare combination of a young, highly educated, self-employed population that is the natural audience for a vinyl-and-coffee hybrid built around lingering, listening parties, and local-artist showcases. Washington County can be considered for a future secondary site given its high incomes and comparable education, but its more suburban age and employment profile is a weaker fit for the daytime remote-worker traffic the cafe depends on.

sections.title: Finding the 20-45 Sweet Spot: Age Concentration by ZIP
sections.subtitle: Ranking Portland ZIP codes by their share of residents in the target 20-45 band
sections.description:
Spinback's core customer — music enthusiasts aged 20-45 who linger over coffee, attend listening parties, and browse crates — is not evenly spread across the metro. Using the age distribution data reported at the ZIP level, we combined the 20s, 30s, and 40s age brackets to approximate the target 20-45 age band and ranked every ZIP code by that combined share of residents.

The concentration is striking. The inner-eastside and close-in central ZIPs dominate. 97214 (Buckman/inner Southeast) leads with 63.0% of residents in their 20s-40s (18.5% in 20s, 27.8% in 30s, 16.7% in 40s), followed closely by 97209 (Pearl District) at 67.9% (23.4% + 30.6% + 13.9%) and 97227 (inner North/Boise-Eliot) at 64.0% (17.8% + 32.3% + 13.9%). 97202 (Sellwood/Westmoreland) and 97211 (Northeast/Woodlawn) also over-index, each with more than half of residents in the target band and healthy 20s populations that suggest strong student and young-creative presence.

At the other end, the outer-southeast and outlying suburban-leaning ZIPs — 97224 (34.2%), 97267 (37.2%), and 97236 (42.9%) — carry meaningfully older or more family-skewed profiles, making them lower-priority for a foot-traffic-dependent cafe and listening-party concept.

Business takeaway: For a location decision, the Pearl District (97209), inner Southeast (97214), and inner North/Northeast (97227, 97211, 97212) offer the deepest pool of on-target residents within walking and short-transit distance. These same ZIPs are the most defensible for evening listening parties and weeknight foot traffic, since the 30s bracket — the single largest and most reliably disposable-income cohort — peaks there (30.6% in 97209, 32.3% in 97227, 27.8% in 97214). ZIPs with strong 20s shares (97201 at 27.2%, 97209 at 23.4%, 97205 at 22.3%, 97232 at 20.0%) are prime for student and early-career artist programming and daytime remote-work coffee dwell time.

sections.title: An Educated, Creative Base: Education and Self-Employment by ZIP
sections.subtitle: Mapping where degree-holders and self-employed creatives concentrate across Portland's ZIP codes
sections.description:
Spinback's ideal customer — the music enthusiast, the creative, the remote worker who lingers over coffee — tends to be highly educated and disproportionately self-employed. This section overlays the share of adults holding a bachelor's or graduate degree against the self-employment rate at the ZIP level to find neighborhoods where both signals run hot. The bubble chart plots combined degree attainment (bachelor's + graduate, from Result 3) against self-employment rate (Result 4), with population as bubble size, so the largest, highest-potential trade areas stand out. The companion violin/distribution view shows how self-employment is spread across all ZIPs, contextualizing which areas are true outliers.

Reading the two metrics together, a tight cluster of close-in Portland ZIPs emerges as prime Spinback territory. ZIP 97212 (Irvington/NE) is the strongest single signal: 68.2% of adults hold a bachelor's (35.7%) or graduate (32.5%) degree AND self-employment reaches 19.6% — the highest self-employment rate of any ZIP measured. ZIP 97239 (SW/Hillsdale) pairs the highest combined degree attainment in the dataset (37.4% bachelor's + 38.0% graduate = 75.4%) with a robust 16.0% self-employment rate. ZIP 97214 (inner SE/Buckman) combines 67.1% degree attainment (39.5% bachelor's + 27.6% graduate) with 18.1% self-employment and the highest labor force participation among core creative ZIPs. Rounding out the top tier: 97215 (68.1% degrees, 18.1% self-employed), 97213 (62.5% degrees, 16.7% self-employed), 97202 (64.8% degrees, 17.0% self-employed), 97211 (56.9% degrees, 18.1% self-employed), and 97232 (65.5% degrees, 15.2% self-employed).

In business terms, this is a well-defined bullseye. The inner east side (97214, 97215, 97202, 97212, 97211, 97213, 97232) and the SW pocket around 97239 concentrate exactly the dual profile Spinback is built for: educated tastemakers with the disposable income and cultural appetite for specialty vinyl and curated coffee, plus a heavy freelance/self-employed population who work flexible hours and are the natural weekday-afternoon "lingerers" a cafe-retail hybrid depends on. High self-employment also signals a built-in audience for daytime listening sessions and a supply of local artists for showcases. Conversely, high-population east-side ZIPs like 97236 (22.0% degrees, 12.1% self-employed) and 97233 (18.9% degrees, 11.5% self-employed) score low on both axes — useful to note as lower-fit areas so marketing and any second-location scouting stay focused on the proven cluster. Recommendation: prioritize 97214, 97212, 97202, 97215, and 97239 for the flagship location, event marketing, and artist-outreach efforts.

sections.title: Spending Power for Vinyl and Specialty Coffee: Income by ZIP
sections.subtitle: Where discretionary income and an active, engaged labor force overlap
sections.description:
Vinyl records, turntables, and specialty coffee are discretionary purchases. To price confidently and to decide how heavily to weight premium products (higher-end turntables, limited pressings, single-origin coffee), Spinback needs to know which ZIP codes concentrate genuine spending power alongside an active, working-age population. This section draws on the household income distributions and labor force participation rates in Result 4 to rank the local ZIP codes on discretionary strength.

Two clusters stand out for premium potential. A tier of affluent inner-eastside and close-in ZIPs pairs very high shares of $150k+ households with strong labor force participation: 97212 (Irvington/Alameda) leads with 44.3% of households earning $150k or more and 69.6% labor force participation, followed by 97215 (38.8% at $150k+, 71.4% participation), 97211 (35.2% at $150k+, 74.0% participation), 97239 (34.0% at $150k+, 64.3% participation), and 97213 (32.6% at $150k+, 72.7% participation). 97223 in Washington County also posts 32.7% at $150k+ with 70.2% participation. These are the ZIPs where a premium product mix and confident pricing are best supported.

A second, price-sensitive tier shows meaningfully lower discretionary income and softer participation — notably 97233 (10.1% at $150k+, 60.5% participation), 97236 (17.1% at $150k+, 67.4% participation), and 97216 (15.2% at $150k+, 67.0% participation). In these areas, an entry-level turntable range, used-vinyl bins, and accessible coffee price points will resonate more than premium tiers.

Business takeaway: locate the flagship storefront and premium/listening-party programming toward the high-income, high-participation eastside cluster (97212, 97215, 97211, 97213, 97214), where affluent working-age residents can absorb premium pricing. Use pop-ups, used inventory, and value coffee options to reach the more price-sensitive outer-east ZIPs without over-pricing them out.

sections.title: Priority Neighborhoods and Siting Recommendations
sections.subtitle: Shortlisting Portland ZIP codes that balance target-age density, creative professionals, and spending power
sections.description:
Spinback's ideal home is a ZIP that concentrates three things at once: a heavy 20s-to-40s population (the target 20-45 music enthusiast), a strong base of creative independents proxied by self-employment and college-plus attainment, and enough household spending power to support both vinyl retail and specialty coffee habits. Reading Results 3 and 4 together, four inner-eastside and central ZIPs rise to the top.

97214 (Buckman/inner SE, 27,714 residents, 3,681/sq mi) is the single strongest fit: 63.0% of residents are in their 20s-40s (18.5% + 27.8% + 16.7%), self-employment is elevated at 18.1%, labor-force participation is the highest in the shortlist at 79.4%, and 67.1% hold a bachelor's or graduate degree. Its income base is broad and healthy — 27.5% earn $150k+ while a large middle tier ($35k-$100k) supplies exactly the discretionary-but-not-luxury spenders who buy used vinyl and linger over coffee.

97209 (Pearl District, 22,296 residents) has the densest footprint in the entire dataset at 8,357/sq mi and an extraordinary 67.9% of residents in their 20s-40s (23.4% + 30.6% + 13.9%). Foot traffic and young-adult concentration are unmatched here, though self-employment (14.3%) is more moderate and the lower-income share is larger, reflecting a renter-heavy young population.

97202 (Sellwood-Moreland/inner SE, 43,533 residents, 2,679/sq mi) blends scale with creative density: 51.7% in the 20s-40s bands, the second-highest self-employment at 17.0%, 64.8% college-or-above, and 33.9% of households at $150k+ — a rare combination of a large addressable population and strong spending power.

97212 (NE/Irvington-Alberta area, 28,042 residents, 3,967/sq mi) posts the highest self-employment in the region at 19.6% and the highest advanced-education share (32.5% graduate degrees), alongside the largest $150k+ concentration at 44.3%. This is the affluent-creative anchor of the shortlist.

Secondary candidates worth monitoring include 97211 (18.1% self-employed, 74.0% labor participation, 35.2% at $150k+) and 97232 (75.1% labor participation, 43.7% in the 20s-40s, 15.2% self-employed). By contrast, outer-east ZIPs such as 97233 and 97236 and southern Clackamas ZIPs like 97267 and 97224 show weaker fit — lower target-age concentration, self-employment near or below 12%, and notably lower college attainment — and should be deprioritized for a flagship store-and-cafe.

Recommendation: target a first location in 97214 or 97202 for the best balance of population scale, creative independents, and spend; use 97209 as the high-traffic urban alternative and 97212 as the premium-market option.
